### D3 red team · Question

Event: `9bd3df34bf22e93429919b5d0464bafe` · 2026-09-24T21:44:07Z

> D3 code review, checkpoint 3 (shared runtime). Read in the scratch worktree /tmp/d3cr1, detached at 6dd491c84 (b69b140f8 plus netd's hook); the implementer's tree was not touched. The branch tip 9f0e3fb5c (a WIP of ipd saved at the handoff) is not reviewed here.
> 
> VERDICT: OK after one P1 fix. The overrides' worst-case sizing is wrong, and the documented milestone manifest exceeds the bound. It is a small fix; everything else is sound.
> 
> == P1: Admission::with_overrides and fits miss the real worst case ==
> `open = sum(o.in_flight) + (buckets - #overrides) x default` assumes every override's bucket occupies a slot. But `buckets` caps concurrent buckets regardless of which ones they are. An override smaller than the default (the steward's in_flight 2 < 5) can be absent, and a sixth default bucket takes its slot. Checked with a scratch test, since deleted: Limits{buckets 6, in_flight 5} with overrides sshd 24 and steward 2 is accepted as 46. Then admitting 24 on sshd's badge plus five other account-0 badges at 5 each gives **49 admitted in flight > 48**. So MAX_OPEN_CALLS - 49 = 15 < OPEN_CALL_HEADROOM 16, and the 'leaves the headroom' guarantee fails for exactly the milestone numbers in NAMESPACES (24 + 2 + 4x5 = 46). `fits` has the same flaw per resource: an override with files 0 or state 4 below the default under-counts memory, so the budget can be overcommitted.
> Fix: per resource, worst = sum over overrides of max(o.cap, default), plus (buckets - #overrides) x default, in both with_overrides and fits. Update NAMESPACES' milestone numbers, for example steward in_flight counted as 5: 24 + 5x5 = 49, so sshd 23, or 5 buckets. Add the test above, which fills every slot through the badges in the worst order.
> 
> == Existing servers unaffected (defaults) ==
> - write_or_wait's default is `self.write(..).map(Write::Done)`, and the Twrite arm keeps its order: fid open for write, offset overflow, labels, then the call, then `count <= data.len()`. For a server that doesn't override it, behaviour is identical.
> - `NineServer::new` becomes `with_admission(fs, Admission::new(limits)?, random)`, the same fields.
> - `cap()` with no overrides is `limits.of(resource)`.
> - new_connection's body was split into mint_at unchanged: reserve, fs.minted, commit, and disconnected on failure.
> - The panic handler with no hook set does one atomic swap and returns, then report_panic and process_exit as before.
> - cargo test passes for redoubt-rt (99 tests across its suites), bootfsd, consoled, blkd, keyd and netd, and rv64 builds for netd and consoled.
> 
> == A waiting Twrite gets the same checks as a waiting read ==
> `Write::Wait` becomes `Held::Wait` only after the open-mode, offset and label checks, and nothing has been written. serve_parking hands it back with the T-message intact (tested byte for byte); re-serving re-reads the lend, so a fid clunked meanwhile gives Rerror. Parking is the server's `Parked::park`, charged to the same buckets and shares, deadline and abandonment, so a waiting write can't hold open calls beyond admission any more than a read can. Under `serve` or `serve_with` it becomes MALFORMED, with no side effect.
> P3: there is no test of a labelled caller's write being refused before it can wait, and no serve_parking-level test of a parked Twrite (park, abandon, expire); the answer_in_place tests cover the skeleton half only.
> 
> == mint_rooted / unmint against answer 168 and disconnect ==
> mint_rooted is new_connection's admission (State, then release on error) plus the shared mint_at, so it uses the same table, a badge at or above 2^63, a random id and the same lineage. `unmint(badge)` is `forget(badge)`: the answer-168 rollback new_connection already uses at ninep.rs:537 and 589, releasing fids, State and fs.disconnected. Tests: rooted at the server's node, `..` stops at the root, disconnect frees it, unmint returns State to 0, and the State cap binds.
> Note: mint_rooted doesn't check that the caller holds a connection, or its labels, unlike make_connection's `root(caller, "")`. That's fine for ipd, whose dispatch refuses labelled callers and checks the caller's scope first, but say so in the doc comment: 'the file server has authorised the caller'.
> 
> == The panic hook ==
> Set once (CAS on 0), run once (HOOK_RAN swap), before report_panic, as asked. The transmute of usize to fn() is sound here: PANIC_HOOK only ever holds 0 or `hook as usize`, and fn pointers are usize-sized on both targets. The budget goes 9 to 10, documented. P3s:
> - (a) The run-once flag lets a second panicking thread skip the hook and reach process_exit while the first thread is still inside the hook, so the reset may not happen. Have later panickers wait, bounded, on a HOOK_DONE flag.
> - (b) `run_panic_hook` is `pub`. Any call disarms the real panic path; make it pub(crate) (its test is in the module).
> - (c) Optional: an AtomicPtr<()> with `hook as *mut ()` keeps provenance, which is cleaner for Miri.
> 
> == netd 6dd491c84 ==
> The hook is armed right after Regs::map, before bring-up. panic_reset rebuilds Regs from two atomics and writes STATUS 0, then polls up to RESET_TRIES; it doesn't allocate and is bounded. The register accesses move onto Regs, so the unsafe count stays at 7. P3: `arm_panic_reset` stores PANIC_LEN even when the base CAS failed, so a second call with another mapping would pair the first base with the second length. That would be a latent out-of-mapping write, contradicting the SAFETY claim. Store the length only on success, before the base, or refuse. Still open from checkpoint 2: P2-1, the rx thread returning silently on a wait_irq error.
> 
> == Fuzz (cargo +nightly fuzz, scratch worktree, fresh corpora in /tmp/rtfuzz) ==
> - ninep_server: 2,315,823 runs in 241 s, about 9.6k exec/s, 1,295 edges, 5,808 new units, peak RSS 468 MB, no crash, exit 0.
> - startup: 59,760,724 runs in 121 s, 201 edges, peak RSS 483 MB, no crash, exit 0.
> P3: the ninep_server target's Tree doesn't override write_or_wait and never calls mint_rooted or with_overrides, so none of this commit's new paths are fuzzed. Add a node that waits (for example on odd offsets) and a rooted mint in the op mix.
> 
> == The tests/parked.rs hang: a test race, not a runtime race ==
> The test predates this commit and is unchanged by it. In `parked_calls_are_served_abandoned_and_expired`, A parks a WAIT whose server deadline is LONGEST = 200 ms. B loops on WAKE until one returns woken = 1, sleeping 1 ms and with no bound. Under heavy parallel load, if more than 200 ms passes between A's call being parked and B's successful WAKE, A's call expires (A gets TIMED_OUT), nothing is parked any more, and B spins for ever, so its `.join()` hangs. A different interleaving under load would instead fail the 42 or the '100 + 1' asserts. The runtime is doing what it should. Fix the test: bound B's loop, or stop when the waiter thread has finished (`is_finished()`), and give A's WAIT a much larger LONGEST than the wake loop can take.
> 
> Scope: libs/rt/src/{start.rs, server/*}, the unsafe-budget line and servers/netd only. Additive, with no change to kernel/, model/ or K5 paths.
